limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

limitations: 新项无旧findings/依赖。prepared候选不含未物化Go，已按固定git show补源码至独占阅读副本，临时SSL重读成功。定向核auth/token store/team/probe路由、selector/Health/Smart/Affinity、OpenAI入口/attempt plan/首chunk failover、usage/request trace、config规则DB/DSH写/CLI参数。未全审全部转换器/企业/OAuth/guardrails/MCP/远控/图片/所有查询、全存储加密及npm构建，未运行目标。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: 为需接多个模型/客户端的个人或管理员，在统一入口管理规则、scope和用量，减少重复baseURL/key接线。见[Q01](#research-q01)。
模型认证与team路由、Health/Smart/Affinity/LB、每attempt转换和首chunk前failover、请求/usage关联；DSH为配置接入。见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。

新项无旧findings/依赖。prepared候选不含未物化Go，已按固定git show补源码至独占阅读副本，临时SSL重读成功。定向核auth/token store/team/probe路由、selector/Health/Smart/Affinity、OpenAI入口/attempt plan/首chunk failover、usage/request trace、config规则DB/DSH写/CLI参数。未全审全部转换器/企业/OAuth/guardrails/MCP/远控/图片/所有查询、全存储加密及npm构建，未运行目标。
独立Go网关，CLI npm manifest 1.6.1、MPL-2.0，源码Go1.26/local replace；固定源码不证明当前npm/全部平台binary对应或作者生产/性能声明。
平台binary/本地DB与配置、token/scope、对应上游/客户端，源构建另需Go/local模块，DSH apply先备原件；表见[Q05](#research-q05)。
网关/日志DB、上游多attempt与OAuth维护，配置/权限和恢复人工未知；表见[Q05](#research-q05)。
熟悉凭据/规则的管理员可localhost隔离渐进小样；身份/协议/规则不符、scope或DSH部分写不明时停扩流/自动配置，核attempt和文件、退原endpoint/副本。见[Q05](#research-q05)。
接线/角色/首chunk与路径观察有据，真实任务正确性、团队隔离全貌、延迟及净费用未测；表见[Q05](#research-q05)。
实际auth后剥probe头、首chunk闸/有限尝试、分区亲和与record关联可借鉴；degrade/未知quota、日志片段与两文件写入边界需显式保留。见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
把角色scope/分区亲和与异构failover/观察接成统一管理路径，有首chunk不混流和非global probe剥头等明确边界。见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
degrade可保不健康候选，首chunk后不重试、quota非硬财务限额、usage非全厂商扣费；DSH两文件备份直写非事务，团队全路径隔离未验。见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
未验证方向是在既有timeline/usage之上加政策版本/客户端语义核对，比较误scope/错路/消费未知和定位负担，现trace充分则否定。见[Q06](#research-q06)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)已有网关/协议/团队模式组合novelty小幅9；[Q02](#research-q02)角色与[Q03](#research-q03)分区亲和/首chunk异构回退是实质mechanism15，非新模型算法23；剥probe与流式提交边界可条件迁移10；统一接线实质简化8但运维成本限制更高。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)多客户端/团队集中管理是实质workflow18；[Q04](#research-q04)请求路径/用量为运维交付改善8，非任务合格或结算新交付15；客户端/协议接入reach小幅5；[Q05](#research-q05)没有净支出/总工时对照economics0，不把cost路由视省钱。

recommendation.reason: 需要集中多个模型和客户端、能管理凭据与规则的个人或团队管理员，可先在 localhost 和独立副本配置中接模拟上游或无价值单 provider 小样。它比逐客户端直连多统一协议、scope、选路与请求观察，但兼容和团队全路径隔离仍需验收，重试与 quota 观察也不保证费用硬上限。身份、协议或规则不符以及 DSH 两文件部分写入无法核恢复时，应停扩流和自动配置，查看实际尝试与文件后退回原 endpoint 或副本。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)多端点/客户端及[Q02](#research-q02)team核心链说明反复接线/归属摩擦，超泛用途15；真实需求频率/原办法不足无独立对照，不到30。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)角色/probe边界与[Q03](#research-q03)真实转换/首chunk回退超入口6；全协议/生产与净收益未测，degrade/多attempt边界阻到19。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)认证/team/probe前后链、[Q03](#research-q03)真实失败/commit与[Q04](#research-q04)DB/DSH写和记录直接核超摘要6；未运行/非全协议或安全审计，不到19。

cost.rationale: [Q05](#research-q05)localhost/单provider/模拟与DB+配置副本/原endpoint退路使负担条件清晰高于不明5；[Q04](#research-q04)多状态/凭据/协议运维和两文件恢复仍专业，非较轻15。

publication.summaries.text: 独立统一模型网关，为多客户端和团队提供协议转换、模型选路、凭据与团队 key 管理，以及请求路径和用量观察。

items.Host 路由: 独立模型API/管理服务，非DSH宿主插件
items.界面: 模型/团队/规则/请求管理Web UI

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 统一端点/转换 | 多客户端接多provider | 具体协议/工具语义需验，非any-to-any已证 |
| 角色/scope | 管理/模型/团队key | 核心路由可核，全数据隔离非已审 |
| 选路/亲和 | 健康/内容/分区/策略选择 | 全不健康degrade，quota未知可pass |
| failover | 首chunk前异构回退 | committed后不重试，尝试可能消费 |
| 观察/DSH接入 | timeline/usage与配置自动写 | 非全部账单，DSH双文件非事务 |

publication.advice.text: 熟悉凭据/规则的管理员可localhost隔离渐进小样；身份/协议/规则不符、scope或DSH部分写不明时停扩流/自动配置，核attempt和文件、退原endpoint/副本。见[Q05](#research-q05)。

href=\"https://github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/issues\">Issues</a>\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-1.26+-00ADD8?style=flat&logo=go\" alt=\"Go Version\" />\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MPL%202.0-brightgreen.svg\" alt=\"License\" />\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Windows-lightgrey\" alt=\"Platform\" />\n</p>\n\nTingly Box **connects any agent to any model** — for you and your whole team, with built-in power-ups.\n\n## Key Features\n\n* **Any Agent ⇄ Any Model**\n  * Unified endpoint for AI — bridge any providers, with protocols translated both ways\n  * One-click config for Agents — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Xcode, and more\n  * Profiles for Claude Code — switch models for different scenarios\n  * Both API keys and OAuth — use your existing quotas anywhere\n  * Smart Routing — route across models and tokens by cost, speed, or custom policies\n* **Team AI Management**\n  * Shared team endpoint with centrally managed model rules\n  * Dedicated keys per member, with data isolated per user\n  * Per-member usage tracking\n* **Power-ups**\n  * Guardrails, MCP Gateway, and Usage Analytics\n  * Image API — image generation and editing through the same gateway, with a built-in playground\n  * Remote Control — drive agents via Telegram, Weixin, WeCom, Feishu, Lark, and DingTalk\n* **Production-Ready**\n  * VModel (Virtual Model) — for testing, validation, and benchmarking\n  * Harness-driven for robustness across protocols, routing, and clients\n  * UX-first visual management of providers, models, team, and remote bots\n  * Blazing fast — typically adds **< 1ms** of overhead\n\n## Preview\n\n![Tingly Box Web UI Demo](./docs/images/output.gif)\n\n## Quick Start\n\n[English](https://github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/issues/678#issuecomment-4273812882) | [中文](https://github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/issues/678#issue-4244345496) | [Fault Record](https://github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/discussions/626)\n\n### Install\n\n<details open>\n<summary><strong>Install globally with npm (recommended)</strong></summary>\n\n```bash\nnpm install -g tingly-box@latest   # --registry=<mirror> works here too\n\ntb start   # tb = tingly-box; runs in the background (--no-daemon for foreground)\ntb open    # open the web UI\n\n# update: reinstall, then restart to apply\nnpm install -g tingly-box@latest\ntb restart\n```\n\n> if any trouble, please check tingly-box output, or call for an issue to help.\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Run with npx</strong></summary>\n\n```bash\n# One command: fetch, restart the server in the background, migrate and open the web UI\n# (a golang binary release; npx wraps the cli for convenience)\nnpx tingly-box@latest\n\n# or -y for convenience\nnpx -y tingly-box@latest\n\n# the binary for your platform comes from npm too (no GitHub download),\n# so an npm mirror is all you need for CN (one of below)\nnpx --registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com -y tingly-box@latest\nnpx --registry=https://mirrors.huaweicloud.com/repository/npm/ -y tingly-box@latest\nnpx --registry=http://mirrors.tencent.com/npm/ -y tingly-box@latest\n```\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Install Node & NPX</strong></summary>\n\n```\n# MacOS & Linux\n## Install Node.js LTS via nvm\ncurl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/master/install.sh | bash\n\n## Restart terminal or load nvm\nsource ~/.nvm/nvm.sh\n\n## Install Node.js LTS\nnvm install --lts\n\n## Verify installation\nnode -v\nnpx -v\n```\n\n```\n# Windows\n## Powershell with Winget\nwinget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS\n\n## Restart terminal, then verify installation\nnode -v\nnpx -v\n\n## Or download and install Node.js LTS manually:\nhttps://nodejs.org/en/download\n```\n\n</details>\n\n<details open>\n<summary><strong>From Docker (GitHub Host)</strong></summary>\n\n```bash\nmkdir tingly-data\ndocker run -d \\\n  --name tingly-box \\\n  -p 12580:12580 \\\n  -v `pwd`/tingly-data:/home/tingly/.tingly-box \\\n  ghcr.io/tingly-dev/tingly-box\n```\n\n</details>\n\nFor Docker Compose (recommended for isolated env), building your own image, or troubleshooting — see the [Docker Guide](./docs/docker.md).\n\n### Integration Guide\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Agent Integration - Claude Code / Claude Desktop / OpenCode / Codex / Xcode / VSCode / OpenClaw</strong></summary>\n\n- Claude Code (support 1-click config)\n- OpenCode (support 1-click config)\n- Xcode (require manual config)\n- ……\n\nAny application is ready to use.\n\n> We've provided detailed config guide in application\n\n![Agent Integration Demo](./docs/images/1-2-claude-code.png)\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Team - Shared Model Deployment</strong></summary>\n\nGive your whole team one endpoint backed by centrally managed model rules. Each member gets a dedicated Team Key, and usage is tracked per user.\n\n1. Open Web UI like `http://localhost:12580`\n2. Navigate to **Team**, configure the model rules, then hand out keys via **Team Keys**\n3. Track per-user consumption under **Dashboard → Team usage**\n\n![Team Demo](./docs/images/2-1-team.png)\n\n![Team Usage Demo](./docs/images/4-1-team-usage.png)\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Image API</strong></summary>\n\nRoute image generation and editing through the same gateway. Point any OpenAI-compatible image client at `http://localhost:12580/tingly/imagegen` and pick the upstream image models with rules, like any other scenario. Try prompts right away in **Image → Playground**.\n\n![Image Playground Demo](./docs/images/3-1-image-playground.png)\n\n![Image API Demo](./docs/images/3-2-image-api.png)\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>DeepSeek Best Compatibility</strong></summary>\n\nDeepSeek is optimized for mainstream agent workflows, offering broad compatibility across protocol adapters, agent clients, extended context, vision, web search, and cache optimization.\n\n| Module                           |      Status | What It Solves                                                        |\n| -------------------------------- | ----------: | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Model List                       | ✅ Supported | Keeps the official model list up to date in real time                 |\n| Protocol Adaptation              | ✅ Supported | Supports official Anthropic/OpenAI APIs with bidirectional conversion |\n| Reasoning Capability             | ✅ Supported | Provides compatibility with Thinking workflows                        |\n| Cache Hit Optimization           | ✅ Supported | Improves cache hit rates for DeepSeek requests                        |\n| Vision Proxy                     | ✅ Supported | Enables DeepSeek to understand and process images                     |\n| Web Search                       | ✅ Supported | Calls official Web tools through the Anthropic endpoint               |\n| 1M Context Window                | ✅ Supported | Enables one-click setup for 1M context                                |\n| Codex Adaptation                 | ✅ Supported | Ensures compatibility with mainstream agent workflows                 |\n| Claude Code / Desktop Adaptation | ✅ Supported | Ensures compatibility with mainstream agent workflows                 |\n\nSupports one-click configuration where available. For applications that require manual setup, detailed in-app configuration guides are provided.\n\nAny compatible application is ready to use.\n\n> Detailed configuration guides are available inside each application.\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Remote Control Agent via IM Bots - TG / DingTalk / Feishu / Lark / Weixin / WeCom</strong></summary>\n\nTingly Box now supports remote control through popular IM platforms. Interact with your AI agents remotely without direct server access.\n\n**Supported Platforms**\n\n- ✅ Telegram\n- ✅ DingTalk\n- ✅ Feishu\n- ✅ Lark\n- ✅ Weixin\n- ✅ WeCom\n\n**Quick Setup**\n\n1. Open Web UI like `http://localhost:12580`\n2. Turn on **Projects** under **Power-ups** in the gear menu at the bottom of the left rail, then open **IM** in the rail\n3. Configure your preferred IM platform bot\n4. Start interacting with your agents remotely\n\n**Use Cases**\n\n- Execute tasks and queries from your phone or any device\n- Team collaboration with shared agent access\n- Monitor and control agents while away from your workstation\n\n![Remote Control Demo](./docs/images/5-1-remote.png)\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>OpenAI SDK</strong></summary>\n\n```python\nfrom openai import OpenAI\n\nclient = OpenAI(\n    api_key=\"your-tingly-model-token\",\n    base_url=\"http://localhost:12580/tingly/openai/v1\"\n)\n\nresponse = client.chat.completions.create(\n    model=\"tingly-gpt\",\n    messages=[{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Hello!\"}]\n)\nprint(response)\n```\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Anthropic SDK</strong></summary>\n\n```python\nfrom anthropic import Anthropic\n\nclient = Anthropic(\n    api_key=\"your-tingly-model-token\",\n    base_url=\"http://localhost:12580/tingly/anthropic\"\n)\n\nresponse = client.messages.create(\n    model=\"tingly\",\n    max_tokens=1024,\n    messages=[\n        {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Hello!\"}\n    ]\n)\nprint(response)\n```\n\n> Tingly Box proxies requests transparently for SDKs and CLI tools.\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Using OAuth Providers</strong></summary>\n\nYou can also add OAuth providers (like Claude Code) and use your existing quota in any OpenAI-compatible tool:\n\n```bash\n# 1. Add Claude Code via OAuth in Web UI (http://localhost:12580)\n# 2. Configure your tool with Tingly Box endpoint\n```\n\nRequests route through your OAuth-authorized provider, using your existing Claude Code quota instead of requiring a separate API key.\n\nThis works with any tool that supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints: Cherry Studio, VS Code extensions, or custom AI agents.\n\n![OAuth Provider Demo](./docs/images/6-1-connect-ai.png)\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Self-Hosted Model Servers - vLLM / SGLang / Ollama / LM Studio / LocalAI / Jan</strong></summary>\n\nAlready running your own inference server? Tingly Box connects to it like any other provider and exposes it through the same unified gateway.\n\n**Supported out of the box**\n\n- vLLM\n- SGLang\n- Ollama\n- LM Studio\n- LocalAI\n- Jan\n\nAnything else that speaks an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API still works via **Custom endpoint**.\n\n**Quick Setup**\n\n1. Open Web UI like `http://localhost:12580`\n2. Click **Connect AI** → pick your engine from the **Self-hosted** section (default URL and key are pre-filled)\n3. **Test Connection**, then save — it's now usable like any other provider\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Web Management UI</strong></summary>\n\nLaunch the web management interface:\n\n```bash\nnpx tingly-box@latest\n```\n\nThen open `http://localhost:12580` in your browser.\n\n![Dashboard](./docs/images/4-2-dashboard.png)\n\n</details>\n\n## Documentation\n\n**[User Manual](./docs/user-manual.md)** – Installation, configuration, and operational guide\n\n**[Docker Guide](./docs/docker.md)** – Building, running, and troubleshooting the Docker images\n\n**[Guardrails](./docs/guardrails.md)** – Policy-based safety checks, built-in protections, and protected credential masking\n\n**[MCP Web Tools](./docs/mcp-web-tools.md)** – Local stdio MCP server for `web_search` / `web_fetch`\n\n## Contributing\n\nBy contributing to this repository, you agree that your contributions may be\nincluded in this project under the MPL-2.0 and may also be used by Tingly Inc.\nunder separate commercial licensing terms.\n\nSee CONTRIBUTING.md and NOTICE for details.\n\n---\n\nWe welcome contributions! Check the steps below to build from source code.\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>Contributing Guide — Build & Dev</strong></summary>\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n| Tool    | Version | Install                                                                                       |\n| ------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Go      | 1.26+   | https://go.dev/doc/install                                                                    |\n| Node.js | 20+     | https://nodejs.org/                                                                           |\n| pnpm    | latest  | `npm install -g pnpm`                                                                         |\n| task    | latest  | `go install github.com/go-task/task/v3/cmd/task@latest` or https://taskfile.dev/installation/ |\n\n> Tip: you can also copy individual shell commands out of `Taskfile.yml` and run them directly if you prefer not to install `task`.\n\n### 1. Clone and init submodules\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box.git\ncd tingly-box\ngit submodule update --init --recursive\n```\n\n### 2. Frontend development\n\nThe frontend is a React + Vite app located in `frontend/`. You can work on it independently of the Go backend.\n\n> **Login token:** the frontend requires an auth token to log in. When the backend starts it prints the full login URL (e.g. `Web UI: http://localhost:12580/login/<token>`). If you need to retrieve it later, run:\n> ```bash\n> tingly-box token view auth --reveal\n> ```\n\n**Mock mode** – no running backend required, uses built-in fixture data:\n\n```bash\ntask web:mock\n# or directly:\ncd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm dev:mock\n```\n\nOpen http://localhost:9245 in your browser. Use the token obtained above to log in.\n\n**Dev mode** – proxies API calls to a local backend (start the backend first, see step 3):\n\n```bash\ntask web\n# or directly:\ncd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm dev\n```\n\n### 3. Backend development\n\nRun the Go server (hot-reload via `go run`):\n\n```bash\ntask start\n# or directly:\ngo run ./cli/tingly-box --verbose start --debug --port 12580 --browser=false\n```\n\nOpen http://localhost:12580 in your browser (serves the last built frontend bundle).\n\n### 4. Full build (frontend + backend binary)\n\nBuilds the frontend, embeds it into the binary, then compiles Go:\n\n```bash\ntask build\n```\n\nThe output binary is written to `./build/tingly-box`.\n\n### 5. GUI binary (Wails) *(optional)*\n\n> The GUI build is not yet publicly released. Skip this step unless you are specifically working on the desktop app.\n\n```bash\ntask wails:build\n```\n\n### Other useful commands\n\n```bash\ntask swagger        # Regenerate openapi.json from Go source\ntask codegen        # Regenerate frontend API client from openapi.json\ntask go:test        # Run Go unit tests\n```\n\n</details>\n\n## Sponsors\n\nIf Tingly Box has been useful to you, consider supporting its development.\n\n**Donations are optional.** A ⭐ on GitHub or a contribution is just as appreciated.\n\n<div align=\"left\">\n\n|   Sponsor   |                Details                |\n| :---------: | :-----------------------------------: |\n| 0xbeekeeper |             First Sponsor             |\n|  richardxx  | Long Term Claude Subscription Support |\n| huajiankan  |      Figma Subscription Support       |\n\n</div>\n\n<div align=\"left\">\n\n| Github Sponsors                                             |                                                            WeChat                                                             |                                                          Alipay                                                           |\n| :---------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | :-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: |\n| ❤️ [Github Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/tingly-dev) | <img src=\"https://github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/blob/main/docs/donation/wechat.jpg?raw=true\" width=\"100\" alt=\"WeChat Pay\"> | <img src=\"https://github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/blob/main/docs/donation/alipay.jpg?raw=true\" width=\"100\" alt=\"Alipay\"> |\n\n</div>\n\n## Contributors\n\n<br />\n\n<table border=\"0\" cellpadding=\"0\" cellspacing=\"0\" style=\"border:none;       "path": "internal/command/options/server_options.go",
      "content": "package options\n\nimport (\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\t\"github.com/spf13/cobra\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/appconfig\"\n)\n\n// StartFlags holds flags for starting the server\ntype StartFlags struct {\n\tPort                 int\n\tHost                 string\n\tEnableUI             bool\n\tEnableDebug          bool\n\tEnableOpenBrowser    bool\n\tEnableStyleTransform bool\n\tDaemon               bool\n\tLogFile              string\n\tProjectsDir          string\n}\n\n// StartServerOptions contains resolved options for starting the server\ntype StartServerOptions struct {\n\tHost              string\n\tPort              int\n\tEnableUI          bool\n\tEnableDebug       bool\n\tEnableOpenBrowser bool\n\tDaemon            bool\n\tLogFile           string\n\t// RecordDir is where scenario recording sinks write when the scenario's\n\t// recording_v2 flag enables recording. Always the config-dir default —\n\t// recording enablement is flag-driven, not a CLI concern.\n\tRecordDir string\n\t// ProjectsDir is where Projects keeps its data: --projects-dir, else\n\t// \"<config dir>-project\", beside the config dir and never inside it.\n\tProjectsDir string\n}\n\n// AddStartFlags adds all start-related flags to a command\n// This is shared between start, restart, gui, and slim commands\nfunc AddStartFlags(cmd *cobra.Command, flags *StartFlags) {\n\tcmd.Flags().IntVarP(&flags.Port, \"port\", \"p\", 0, \"Server port (default: from config or 12580)\")\n\tcmd.Flags().StringVar(&flags.Host, \"host\", \"localhost\", \"Server host\")\n\tcmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&flags.EnableUI, \"ui\", \"u\", true, \"Enable web UI (default: true)\")\n\tcmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flags.EnableDebug, \"debug\", false, \"Enable debug mode including gin, low level logging and so on (default: false)\")\n\tcmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flags.EnableOpenBrowser, \"browser\", true, \"Auto-open browser when server starts (default: true)\")\n\tcmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flags.EnableStyleTransform, \"adapter\", true, \"Enable API style transformation (default: true)\")\n\tcmd.Flags().BoolVar(&flags.Daemon, \"daemon\", false, \"Run as daemon in background (default: false)\")\n\tcmd.Flags().StringVar(&flags.LogFile, \"log-file\", \"\", \"Log file path for daemon mode (default: ~/.tingly-box/tingly-box.log)\")\n}\n\n// ResolveStartOptions resolves CLI flags with config file defaults\n// Priority: CLI flag > Config > Default\nfunc ResolveStartOptions(cmd *cobra.Command, flags StartFlags, appConfig *appconfig.AppConfig) StartServerOptions {\n\t// Apply priority: CLI flag > Config > Default\n\tresolvedDebug := flags.EnableDebug\n\tif !cmd.Flags().Changed(\"debug\") {\n\t\tresolvedDebug = appConfig.GetDebug()\n\t}\n\n\tresolvedPort := flags.Port\n\tif resolvedPort == 0 {\n\t\tresolvedPort = appConfig.GetServerPort()\n\t} else {\n\t\tappConfig.SetServerPort(flags.Port)\n\t}\n\n\t// Priority: --projects-dir (remembered) > remembered value > default\n\tresolvedProjectsDir := flags.ProjectsDir\n\tif resolvedProjectsDir != \"\" {\n\t\tif err := appConfig.SetProjectsDir(resolvedProjectsDir); err != nil {\n\t\t\tlogrus.Warnf(\"Failed to remember --projects-dir: %v\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t} else if resolvedProjectsDir = appConfig.GetProjectsDir(); resolvedProjectsDir == \"\" {\n\t\tresolvedProjectsDir = DefaultProjectsDir(appConfig.ConfigDir())\n\t}\n\n\treturn StartServerOptions{\n\t\tHost:              flags.Host,\n\t\tPort:              resolvedPort,\n\t\tEnableUI:          flags.EnableUI,\n\t\tEnableDebug:       resolvedDebug,\n\t\tEnableOpenBrowser: flags.EnableOpenBrowser,\n\t\tDaemon:            flags.Daemon,\n\t\tLogFile:           flags.LogFile,\n\t\tRecordDir:         appConfig.ConfigDir() + \"/record\",\n\t\tProjectsDir:       resolvedProjectsDir,\n\t}\n}\n\n// DefaultProjectsDir is the Projects data directory of the instance whose\n// config directory is configDir: a sibling named \"<config dir>-project\"\n// (~/.tingly-box-project by default), so instances never share a database\n// and a thread's working directory never sits next to the config.\nfunc DefaultProjectsDir(configDir string) string {\n\treturn filepath.Clean(configDir) + \"-project\"\n}\n"

      "path": "internal/server/server_routes.go",
      "content": "package server\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/middleware\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/server/module\"\n\tsharing \"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/server/module/sharing\"\n\tteam \"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/server/module/team\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/swagger\"\n)\n\n// setupMiddleware configures server middleware\nfunc (s *Server) setupMiddleware() {\n\t// Memory log middleware for HTTP request logging\n\tif s.memoryLogMW != nil {\n\t\ts.engine.Use(s.memoryLogMW.Middleware())\n\t}\n\t// Recover inside access logging so panics retain their error and 500 status.\n\ts.engine.Use(middleware.Recovery())\n\n\t// CORS middleware\n\ts.engine.Use(middleware.CORS())\n}\n\n// setupRoutes configures server routes\nfunc (s *Server) setupRoutes(ctx context.Context) {\n\n\ts.UseAIEndpoints()\n\n\ts.UseLoadBalanceEndpoints()\n\n\t// Multi-tenant token management API\n\ts.UseTokenManagementEndpoints()\n\n\t// Virtual model endpoints for testing\n\ts.UseVirtualModelEndpoints()\n\n\t// Integrate Web UI routes if enabled\n\tif s.enableUI {\n\t\ts.UseUIEndpoints(ctx)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (s *Server) UseAIEndpoints() {\n\t// The gateway route shape (/tingly/:scenario[/v1]/...) is owned by\n\t// protocolserver; the host only supplies the engine and model auth.\n\ts.aiHandler.RegisterRoutes(s.engine, s.getModelAuthMiddleware())\n}\n\n// UseVirtualModelEndpoints sets up the direct virtual-model entrypoints,\n// split per protocol:\n//\n//\t/virtual/openai/v1/{models,chat/completions,responses}\n//\t/virtual/anthropic/v1/{models,messages}\n//\n// These bypass the provider/rule/scenario pipeline and call the in-process\n// handler directly — useful when a client wants a fixed URL pointed at the\n// vmodel registry without configuring a provider. The protocol split\n// ensures /models returns only the model IDs the chosen protocol can\n// actually dispatch.\n//\n// The canonical path for virtual models in normal use is still\n// /v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions, where a vmodel provider is dispatched\n// like any other provider: through the SDK to the private in-memory\n// virtualserver listener (see .design/vmodel-transport.md).\nfunc (s *Server) UseVirtualModelEndpoints() {\n\tmw := s.getModelAuthMiddleware()\n\n\topenai := s.engine.Group(\"/virtual/openai\")\n\topenai.Use(mw)\n\ts.virtualModelService.SetupOpenAIRoutes(openai)\n\n\tanthropic := s.engine.Group(\"/virtual/anthropic\")\n\tanthropic.Use(mw)\n\ts.virtualModelService.SetupAnthropicRoutes(anthropic)\n}\n\nfunc (s *Server) UseLoadBalanceEndpoints() {\n\t// API routes for load balancer management\n\tapi := s.engine.Group(\"/api/v1/load-balancer\")\n\tapi.Use(s.getUserAuthMiddleware()) // Require user authentication for management APIs\n\n\t// Load balancer API routes\n\ts.loadBalancerAPI.RegisterRoutes(api)\n}\n\n// UseTokenManagementEndpoints registers the token management API endpoints.\nfunc (s *Server) UseTokenManagementEndpoints() {\n\tif s.config == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tsm := s.config.StoreManager()\n\tif sm == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tstore := sm.APIToken()\n\tif store == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tmanager := swagger.NewRouteManager(s.engine)\n\tapi := manager.NewGroup(\"api\", \"v1\", \"\")\n\tapi.Router.Use(s.getUserAuthMiddleware())\n\tmodule.Mount(&module.Routes{V1: api, Engine: s.engine, Manager: manager},\n\t\tsharing.NewHandler(store), team.NewHandler(sm.Team()))\n}\n"

(\n\t\"crypto/rsa\"\n\t\"crypto/x509\"\n\t\"encoding/pem\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"net/http\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"time\"\n\n\t\"github.com/gin-gonic/gin\"\n\t\"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/config\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/constant\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/db\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/pkg/auth\"\n)\n\n// AuthMiddleware provides authentication middleware for different types of authentication\ntype AuthMiddleware struct {\n\tconfig          *config.Config\n\tjwtManager      *auth.JWTManager\n\tapiTokenManager *auth.APITokenManager\n\tapiTokenStore   APITokenStore\n}\n\n// APITokenStore interface for token validation (abstracted for testability)\ntype APITokenStore interface {\n\tValidateToken(tokenID string) (*db.APITokenRecord, error)\n\tUpdateLastUsed(tokenID string) error\n}\n\n// ErrorResponse represents an error response\ntype ErrorResponse struct {\n\tError ErrorDetail `json:\"error\"`\n}\n\n// abortWithError sends an error response and adds the error to gin context for logging\nfunc abortWithError(c *gin.Context, statusCode int, message string, errorType string) {\n\t// Add error to context so logging middleware can capture it\n\tc.Error(fmt.Errorf(\"%s: %s\", errorType, message)).SetType(gin.ErrorTypePublic)\n\n\t// Send JSON response\n\tc.JSON(statusCode, ErrorResponse{\n\t\tError: ErrorDetail{\n\t\t\tMessage: message,\n\t\t\tType:    errorType,\n\t\t},\n\t})\n\tc.Abort()\n}\n\n// ErrorDetail represents error details\ntype ErrorDetail struct {\n\tMessage string `json:\"message\"`\n\tType    string `json:\"type\"`\n\tCode    string `json:\"code,omitempty\"`\n}\n\n// NewAuthMiddleware creates a new authentication middleware\nfunc NewAuthMiddleware(cfg *config.Config, jwtManager *auth.JWTManager, apiTokenManager *auth.APITokenManager, apiTokenStore APITokenStore) *AuthMiddleware {\n\treturn &AuthMiddleware{\n\t\tconfig:          cfg,\n\t\tjwtManager:      jwtManager,\n\t\tapiTokenManager: apiTokenManager,\n\t\tapiTokenStore:   apiTokenStore,\n\t}\n}\n\ntype enterpriseContextClaims struct {\n\tUserID       string\n\tDepartmentID string\n\tKeyPrefix    string\n\tTier         string\n\tJTI          string\n}\n\nfunc containsFold(items []string, target string) bool {\n\tfor _, item := range items {\n\t\tif strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(item), strings.TrimSpace(target)) {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\nfunc resolveSecretRef(raw string) (string, error) {\n\tref := strings.TrimSpace(raw)\n\tif ref == \"\" {\n\t\treturn \"\", nil\n\t}\n\tif strings.HasPrefix(ref, \"env:\") {\n\t\treturn strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(ref, \"env:\")))), nil\n\t}\n\tif strings.HasPrefix(ref, \"file:\") {\n\t\tpath := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(ref, \"file:\"))\n\t\tcontent, err := os.ReadFile(path)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", err\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn strings.TrimSpace(string(content)), nil\n\t}\n\tif st, err := os.Stat(ref); err == nil && !st.IsDir() {\n\t\tcontent, readErr := os.ReadFile(ref)\n\t\tif readErr != nil {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", readErr\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn strings.TrimSpace(string(content)), nil\n\t}\n\treturn ref, nil\n}\n\nfunc parseRSAPublicKeyFromPEM(raw string) (*rsa.PublicKey, error) {\n\tblock, _ := pem.Decode([]byte(raw))\n\tif block == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"invalid pem block\")\n\t}\n\tif key, err := x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey(block.Bytes); err == nil {\n\t\trsaKey, ok := key.(*rsa.PublicKey)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"public key is not RSA\")\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn rsaKey, nil\n\t}\n\tcert, certErr := x509.ParseCertificate(block.Bytes)\n\tif certErr == nil {\n\t\tif rsaKey, ok := cert.PublicKey.(*rsa.PublicKey); ok {\n\t\t\treturn rsaKey, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil, errors.New(\"failed to parse rsa public key\")\n}\n\nfunc verifyEnterpriseContextJWT(cfg *config.Config, rawToken string) (*enterpriseContextClaims, error) {\n\ttokenString := strings.TrimSpace(rawToken)\n\tif tokenString == \"\" || cfg == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\tjwtCfg := cfg.EnterpriseContextJWT\n\tif !jwtCfg.Enabled {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\tclockSkew := time.Duration(jwtCfg.ClockSkewSeconds) * time.Second\n\tparsed, err := jwt.Parse(tokenString, func(token *jwt.Token) (interface{}, error) {\n\t\talg := strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(token.Method.Alg()))\n\t\tif len(jwtCfg.AlgAllowlist) > 0 && !containsFold(jwtCfg.AlgAllowlist, alg) {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"algorithm %s is not allowed\", alg)\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch alg {\n\t\tcase \"HS256\":\n\t\t\tsecret, secretErr := resolveSecretRef(jwtCfg.HS256SecretRef)\n\t\t\tif secretErr != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, secretErr\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif strings.TrimSpace(secret) == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"hs256 secret is empty\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treturn []byte(secret), nil\n\t\tcase \"RS256\":\n\t\t\t// If no public keys were provided, fall back to RS256PublicKeyRef.\n\t\t\tif len(jwtCfg.PublicKeys) == 0 && strings.TrimSpace(jwtCfg.RS256PublicKeyRef) != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tref, refErr := resolveSecretRef(jwtCfg.RS256PublicKeyRef)\n\t\t\t\tif refErr == nil && strings.TrimSpace(ref) != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\t\tif pub, parseErr := parseRSAPublicKeyFromPEM(ref); parseErr == nil {\n\t\t\t\t\t\treturn pub, nil\n\t\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tkid, _ := token.Header[\"kid\"].(string)\n\t\t\tkid = strings.TrimSpace(kid)\n\t\t\tfor _, item := range jwtCfg.PublicKeys {\n\t\t\t\tif kid != \"\" && strings.TrimSpace(item.KID) != kid {\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tpub, parseErr := parseRSAPublicKeyFromPEM(item.PEM)\n\t\t\t\tif parseErr != nil Shared by profileAliasMiddleware\n// and legacyScenarioAliasMiddleware — both need every downstream stage\n// (contextMiddleware, auth, routing, usage records) to see only the\n// canonical form, never the alias a caller actually used.\nfunc rewriteScenarioParam(c *gin.Context, rawScenario, rewritten string) {\n\tfor i := range c.Params {\n\t\tif c.Params[i].Key == \"scenario\" {\n\t\t\tc.Params[i].Value = rewritten\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\toldSeg := \"/tingly/\" + rawScenario\n\tnewSeg := \"/tingly/\" + rewritten\n\trewriteSeg := func(p string) string {\n\t\tif rest, found := strings.CutPrefix(p, oldSeg); found {\n\t\t\treturn newSeg + rest\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn p\n\t}\n\tc.Request.URL.Path = rewriteSeg(c.Request.URL.Path)\n\tif c.Request.URL.RawPath != \"\" {\n\t\tc.Request.URL.RawPath = rewriteSeg(c.Request.URL.RawPath)\n\t}\n}\n\n// legacyScenarioAliasMiddleware rewrites a deprecated scenario id (e.g.\n// \"agent\", renamed to \"custom\") to its canonical id before anything else\n// runs. Additional\n// teams use the isolated internal form \"team:<stable-id>\".\nfunc (ph *ProtocolHandler) teamScopeMiddleware(c *gin.Context) {\n\tif c.Param(\"scenario\") != string(typ.ScenarioTeam) {\n\t\tc.Next()\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tteamID := c.GetString(constant.CtxKeyTeamID)\n\tif teamID == \"\" {\n\t\t// Global model auth has no explicit team claim.       "content": "package routing\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\t\"github.com/gin-gonic/gin\"\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/constant\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/loadbalance\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/typ\"\n)\n\n// SimpleSelector is the production-facing facade over the ServiceSelector\n// pipeline. It adds the probe-pin bypass, gin session/observability plumbing,\n// and debug headers on top of the raw stage pipeline. Request handlers should\n// use it; only diagnostics (e.g. the LB simulator) drive ServiceSelector.Select\n// directly.\ntype SimpleSelector struct {\n\tselector *ServiceSelector\n}\n\n// NewSimpleSelector creates a simplified selector\nfunc NewSimpleSelector(selector *ServiceSelector) *SimpleSelector {\n\treturn &SimpleSelector{selector: selector}\n}\n\n// SelectService resolves the session, runs the selection pipeline, validates\n// the provider, and records the decision (gin context keys, log line, debug\n// headers). The resolved session ID is stored in the gin context.\nfunc (s *SimpleSelector) SelectService(\n\tc *gin.Context,\n\tscenario typ.RuleScenario,\n\trule *typ.Rule,\n\treq interface{},\n) (*typ.Provider, *loadbalance.Service, error) {\n\t// X-Tingly-Probe-Service: {provider_uuid}:{model} — bypass all pipeline\n\t// stages and pin to the specified service. Used by service-target probes\n\t// that need to route through TB's middleware stack (for flag application)\n\t// while targeting a specific provider+model.\n\tif probeService := c.GetHeader(\"X-Tingly-Probe-Service\"); probeService != \"\" {\n\t\tif providerUUID, model, ok := strings.Cut(probeService, \":\"); ok {\n\t\t\tprovider, err := s.selector.config.GetProviderByUUID(providerUUID)\n\t\t\tif err != nil || provider == nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(\"probe service provider not found: %s\", providerUUID)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif !provider.Enabled {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(\"probe service provider disabled: %s\", providerUUID)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tsvc := &loadbalance.Service{Provider: providerUUID, Model: model, Active: true}\n\t\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[routing] probe service pin: provider=%s model=%s\", provider.Name, model)\n\t\t\tsetRoutingDebugHeaders(c, provider.Name, provider.UUID, model, SourceProbePin, -1, nil)\n\t\t\treturn provider, svc, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Build context (session ID resolved internally)\n\tctx := NewSelectionContext(rule, req, c, scenario)\n\n\t// Execute pipeline\n\tresult, err := s.selector.Select(ctx)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tif result.Provider == nil || result.Service == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(\"selection returned nil result\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Automatically store sessionID in gin context for downstream handlers\n\tc.Set(constant.CtxKeySessionID, ctx.SessionID.String())\n\t// The scoped affinity key (session + matched smart partition) — consumers\n\t// that write back to the affinity entry (e.g. message-id updates) must use\n\t// this, not the bare session, or they'll miss partition-scoped pins.\n\tc.Set(constant.CtxKeyAffinityKey, AffinitySessionKey(ctx.SessionID.String(), result.MatchedSmartRuleIndex))\n\n\t// Store LB trajectory: which upstream was selected and via which tactic.\n\t// SourceSmartRouting and SourceAffinity bypass the normal LB tactic, so\n\t// label them explicitly; otherwise use the rule's configured tactic name.\n\tc.Set(constant.CtxKeyLBServiceID, result.Service.ServiceID())\n\ttacticName := result.Source\n\tif result.Source != SourceSmartRouting && result.Source != SourceAffinity {\n\t\ttacticName = rule.GetTacticType().String()\n\t}\n\tc.Set(constant.CtxKeyLBTactic, tacticName)\n\n\tlogrus.WithContext(c.Request.Context()).WithFields(logrus.Fields{\n\t\t\"stage\":            \"routing_selected\",\n\t\t\"rule_uuid\":        rule.UUID,\n\t\t\"scenario\":         string(scenario),\n\t\t\"request_model\":    rule.RequestModel,\n\t\t\"source\":           result.Source,\n\t\t\"lb_tactic\":        tacticName,\n\t\t\"service\":          result.Service.ServiceID(),\n\t\t\"provider\":         result.Provider.Name,\n\t\t\"provider_uuid\":    result.Provider.UUID,\n\t\t\"model\":            result.Service.Model,\n\t\t\"routed_model\":     result.Service.Model,\n\t\t\"routed_provider\":  result.Provider.Name,\n\t\t\"candidate_count\":  len(ctx.Rule.GetActiveServices()),\n\t\t\"evaluated_stages\": result.EvaluatedStages,\n\t}).Infof(\"[routing] selected %s/%s via %s\", result.Provider.UUID, result.Service.Model, result.Source)\n\n\tsetRoutingDebugHeaders(c, result.Provider.Name, result.Provider.UUID, result.Service.Model, result.Source, result.MatchedSmartRuleIndex, result.EvaluatedStages)\n\n\treturn result.Provider, result.Service, nil\n}\n\n// setRoutingDebugHeaders emits X-Tingly-Selected-* response headers describing\n// the routing decision, but only when the request opted in via\n// X-Tingly-Debug-Routing: 1 (set by probes). matchedSmartRule < 0 means none.\nfunc setRoutingDebugHeaders(c *gin.Context, providerName, providerUUID, model, source string, matchedSmartRule int, evaluatedStages []string) {\n\tif c.GetHeader(\"X-Tingly-Debug-Routing\") != \"1\" {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.Header(\"X-Tingly-Selected-Provider\", providerName)\n\tc.Header(\"X-Tingly-Selected-Provider-UUID\", providerUUID)\n\tc.Header(\"X-Tingly-Selected-Model\", model)\n\tc.Header(\"X-Tingly-Routing-Source\", source)\n\tif len(evaluatedStages) > 0 {\n\t\tc.Header(\"X-Tingly-Evaluated-Stages\", strings.Join(evaluatedStages, \",\"))\n\t}\n\tif matchedSmartRule >= 0 {\n\t\tc.Header(\"X-Tingly-Matched-Smart-Rule\", fmt.Sprintf(\"%d\", matchedSmartRule))\n\t}\n}\n\n// SelectServiceForEmbeddings is a variant of SelectService for embedding requests.\n// Embedding requests don't carry chat-style context, so content-based smart routing\n// is skipped (load balancing, affinity, and health filters still apply).\nfunc (s *SimpleSelector) SelectServiceForEmbeddings(\n\tc *gin.Context,\n\tscenario typ.RuleScenario,\n\trule *typ.Rule,\n) (*typ.Provider, *loadbalance.Service, error) {\n\treturn s.SelectService(c, scenario, rule, nil)\n}\n\n// SelectServiceForImageGeneration is a variant of SelectService for image generation\n// requests. Image generation requests don't carry chat-style context, so content-based\n// smart routing is skipped (load balancing, affinity, and health filters still apply).\nfunc (s *SimpleSelector) SelectServiceForImageGeneration(\n\tc *gin.Context,\n\tscenario typ.RuleScenario,\n\trule *typ.Rule,\n) (*typ.Provider, *loadbalance.Service, error) {\n\treturn s.SelectService(c, scenario, rule, nil)\n}\n"

      "path": "internal/routing/selector.go",
      "content": "package routing\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"time\"\n\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\tpkgobs \"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/obs\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/clock\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/loadbalance\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/typ\"\n)\n\n// ProviderResolver resolves providers by UUID and persists config state.\ntype ProviderResolver interface {\n\tGetProviderByUUID(uuid string) (*typ.Provider, error)\n\t// GetEffectiveAffinity returns the effective affinity TTL for a rule,\n\t// considering both scenario default and rule override. Returns 0 if disabled.\n\tGetEffectiveAffinity(rule *typ.Rule) time.Duration\n}\n\n// LoadBalancer defines the interface for load balancing operations.\n// This avoids importing the server package (which would create circular imports).\ntype LoadBalancer interface {\n\tSelectService(rule *typ.Rule) (*loadbalance.Service, error)\n}\n\n// AffinityStore interface defines operations for session-service affinity\ntype AffinityStore interface {\n\tGet(ruleUUID, sessionID string) (*AffinityEntry, bool)\n\tSet(ruleUUID, sessionID string, entry *AffinityEntry)\n\tCountByService(serviceID string) int // count active sessions locked to this service\n}\n\n// AffinityEntry represents a locked service for a session\ntype AffinityEntry struct {\n\tService   *loadbalance.Service\n\tMessageID string\n\tLockedAt  time.Time\n\tExpiresAt time.Time\n}\n\n// ServiceSelector is the main entry point for service selection.\n// It orchestrates a pipeline of selection stages and validates the final result.\ntype ServiceSelector struct {\n\tconfig        ProviderResolver\n\taffinityStore AffinityStore\n\tloadBalancer  LoadBalancer\n\n\t// One pipeline serves every rule — each stage self-guards (see the comment\n\t// in NewServiceSelectorWithLogger). Built once at construction.\n\tpipeline []SelectionStage\n}\n\ntype healthFilterProvider interface {\n\tHealthFilter() *HealthFilter\n}\n\n// initialCandidateServices builds the pipeline's starting candidate set:\n// base ∪ every smart-routing partition's services, deduplicated by service\n// ID (partition entries override a same-ID base entry in place). The union\n// exists so HealthStage — which runs first — can pre-filter partition-only\n// services too (see pipeline-health-before-smart-routing); SmartRoutingStage\n// is responsible for narrowing back down to a single scope (the matched\n// partition, or the base pool when none matches) before handing candidates\n// to Affinity/LoadBalancer, so a service that only exists inside an\n// unmatched partition never reaches the terminal pick.\nfunc initialCandidateServices(rule *typ.Rule) []*loadbalance.Service {\n\tif rule == nil {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Deduplicate services by service ID while preserving first-seen order.\n\t// Map iteration order in Go is randomized, so building the candidate slice\n\t// from a map would make routing (and tests) non-deterministic. We keep an\n\t// ordered slice and use the index map only to dedupe / override in place.\n\tservices := make([]*loadbalance.Service, 0, len(rule.Services))\n\tindexByID := make(map[string]int)\n\n\tadd := func(svc *loadbalance.Service) {\n\t\t// Inactive services are never selectable (every downstream stage and\n\t\t// the final validation reject them), so they must not enter the\n\t\t// candidate set at all: a \"healthy\" inactive entry would keep\n\t\t// HealthStage's all-unhealthy degrade guard from firing and let health\n\t\t// filtering eliminate every selectable service, failing the rule with\n\t\t// \"no active services\" instead of surfacing the real upstream error.\n\t\tif svc == nil || !svc.Active {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tid := svc.GetServiceID().String()\n\t\tif i, ok := indexByID[id]; ok {\n\t\t\t// Override the existing entry in place, keeping its position.\n\t\t\tservices[i] = svc\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tindexByID[id] = len(services)\n\t\tservices = append(services, svc)\n\t}\n\n\t// Add default services.\n\tfor _, svc := range rule.Services {\n\t\tadd(svc)\n\t}\n\n\t// Add smart_routing services (override defaults if same ID).\n\tfor _, sr := range rule.SmartRouting {\n\t\tfor _, svc := range sr.Services {\n\t\t\tadd(svc)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn services\n}\n\n// NewServiceSelector creates a new service selector\nfunc NewServiceSelector(\n\tcfg ProviderResolver,\n\taffinity AffinityStore,\n\tlb LoadBalancer,\n) *ServiceSelector {\n\treturn NewServiceSelectorWithLogger(cfg, affinity, lb, nil)\n}\n\n// NewServiceSelectorWithLogger is like NewServiceSelector but also wires the\n// multi-logger into smart-routing stages so each evaluation is captured to the\n// dedicated smart_routing log source.\nfunc NewServiceSelectorWithLogger(\n\tcfg ProviderResolver,\n\taffinity AffinityStore,\n\tlb LoadBalancer,\n\tmultiLogger *pkgobs.MultiLogger,\n) *ServiceSelector {\n\ts := &ServiceSelector{\n\t\tconfig:        cfg,\n\t\taffinityStore: affinity,\n\t\tloadBalancer:  lb,\n\t}\n\n\tvar healthFilter *HealthFilter\n\tif p, ok := lb.(healthFilterProvider); ok {\n\t\thealthFilter = p.HealthFilter()\n\t}\n\n\tnewSmart := func() *SmartRoutingStage {\n\t\tstage := NewSmartRoutingStage(affinity)\n\t\tif multiLogger != nil {\n\t\t\tstage.SetMultiLogger(multiLogger)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn stage\n\t}\n\n\t// One pipeline serves every rule — order is health → smart → affinity →\n\t// strategy. Each stage self-guards, so there is no need for per-mode\n\t// variants:\n\t//   - Health  narrows the candidate set by 429/auth health; passes through\n\t//     when no filter is set or filtering would empty the set (degrade).\n\t//   - Smart   runs BEFORE affinity: it decides the content partition (and\n\t//     always runs processor ops, which mutate the request) by narrowing\n\t//     the candidate set to the matched subset. Running it after affinity\n\t//     let a first-request pin defeat content routing for the whole\n\t//     session TTL — and skip processor ops entirely for pinned sessions.\n\t//     Passes through when smart routing is off or unmatched.\n\t//   - Affinity returns nothing when affinity is disabled or there's no\n\t//     session. Pins are scoped per matched partition (AffinitySessionKey),\n\t//     so stickiness lives INSIDE the content decision, never above it.\n\t//     The breaker-driven (500) signal is consulted inside the affinity\n\t//     tier check and the tier tactic; Health feeds it the 429/auth signal.\n\t//   - LB      always selects (the terminal fallback) within the narrowed\n\t//     candidate set, labeling the result smart_routing when a partition\n\t//     matched.\n\ts.pipeline = []SelectionStage{\n\t\tNewHealthStage(healthFilter),\n\t\tnewSmart(),\n\t\tNewAffinityStage(affinity),\n\t\tNewLoadBalancerStage(lb),\n\t}\n\n\treturn s\n}\n\n// SetQuotaProvider wires quota lookups into the pipeline's smart\n// routing stage so service_quota ops can compare against provider usage.\n// Optional — call it after construction once a quota manager is available;\n// unset leaves service_quota ops passing through (see QuotaProvider).\nfunc (s *ServiceSelector) SetQuotaProvider(qp QuotaProvider) {\n\tfor _, stage := range s.pipeline {\n\t\tif sm, ok := stage.(*SmartRoutingStage); ok {\n\t\t\tsm.SetQuotaProvider(qp)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// Select is the main entry point for service selection.\n// It picks a pre-built pipeline based on rule configuration and executes it.\nfunc (s *ServiceSelector) Select(ctx *SelectionContext) (*SelectionResult, error) {\n\tcandidates := initialCandidateServices(ctx.Rule)\n\tevaluatedStages := make([]string, 0, len(s.pipeline))\n\n\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[selector] executing pipeline with %d stages for rule %s\",\n\t\tlen(s.pipeline), ctx.Rule.UUID)\n\n\t// Execute pipeline stages in order\n\tfor _, stage := range s.pipeline {\n\t\tstageName := stage.Name()\n\t\tevaluatedStages = append(evaluatedStages, stageName)\n\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[selector] evaluating stage: %s\", stageName)\n\n\t\tnarrowed, result, err := stage.Evaluate(ctx, candidates)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"stage %s: %w\", stageName, err)\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Degrade, don't disappear — enforced once here, between stages, so no\n\t\t// stage ever observes an empty candidate set while the rule still has\n\t\t// active services (see activeBaseFallback). A rule with zero active\n\t\t// services keeps the empty set and the terminal stage reports it.\n\t\tif len(narrowed) == 0 {\n\t\t\tif fallback := activeBaseFallback(ctx, ctx.Rule, \"routing_pipeline_degrade\"); fallback != nil {\n\t\t\t\tnarrowed = fallback\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tcandidates = narrowed\n\n\t\tif result != nil {\n\t\t\t// Attach the cumulative path at the terminal boundary so\n\t\t\t// observability reports every stage that actually ran, including\n\t\t\t// pass-through stages that only narrowed the candidate set.\n\t\t\tresult.EvaluatedStages = append([]string(nil), evaluatedStages...)\n\n\t\t\tif result.Service == nil {\n\t\t\t\tlogrus.Warnf(\"[selector] stage %s returned a final result with a nil service\", stageName)\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// Validate service is active\n\t\t\tif !result.Service.Active {\n\t\t\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[selector] stage %s returned inactive service, trying next stage\", stageName)\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// Resolve provider\n\t\t\tprovider, err := s.config.GetProviderByUUID(result.Service.Provider)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[selector] provider not found for service: %v, trying next stage\", err)\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tif !provider.Enabled {\n\t\t\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[selector] provider %s is disabled, trying next stage\", provider.Name)\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tresult.Provider = provider\n\n\t\t\t// Post-process: lock affinity if needed\n\t\t\ts.postProcess(ctx, result)\n\n\t\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[selector] selected service %s from provider %s via %s\",\n\t\t\t\tresult.Service.Model, provider.Name, result.Source)\n\n\t\t\treturn result, nil\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[selector] stage %s passed to next stage\", stageName)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"no service available for rule %s (model: %s)\",\n\t\tctx.Rule.UUID, ctx.Rule.RequestModel)\n}\n\n// postProcess handles post-selection logic like affinity locking.\n// Locks affinity whenever affinity is enabled and the source is not SourceAffinity\n// (i.e., don't re-lock an already-locked entry).\nfunc (s *ServiceSelector) postProcess(ctx *SelectionContext, result *SelectionResult) {\n\tif result.Source == SourceAffinity || ctx.SessionID.IsEmpty() {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tttl := s.config.GetEffectiveAffinity(ctx.Rule)\n\tif ttl == 0 {\n\t\t// Affinity disabled for this rule.\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\t// Pin inside the partition this request was routed by, so one session can\n\t// hold independent pins per request kind (see AffinitySessionKey).\n\taffinityKey := AffinitySessionKey(ctx.SessionID.String(), ctx.MatchedSmartRuleIndex)\n\ts.affinityStore.Set(ctx.Rule.UUID, affinityKey, &AffinityEntry{\n\t\tService:   result.Service,\n\t\tLockedAt:  clock.Now(),\n\t\tExpiresAt: clock.Now().Add(ttl),\n\t})\n\tlogrus.Infof(\"[affinity] locked service %s -> %s for session key %s\",\n\t\tresult.Provider.Name, result.Service.Model, affinityKey)\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "internal/routing/stage_health.go",
      "content": "package routing\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/loadbalance\"\n)\n\n// HealthStage filters unhealthy services from the context.\n// It runs first and narrows ctx.CandidateServices.\ntype HealthStage struct {\n\tfilter *HealthFilter\n}\n\n// NewHealthStage creates a new health stage with the given health filter\nfunc NewHealthStage(filter *HealthFilter) *HealthStage {\n\treturn &HealthStage{filter: filter}\n}\n\nfunc (s *HealthStage) Name() string {\n\treturn SourceHealth\n}\n\nfunc (s *HealthStage) Evaluate(ctx *SelectionContext, candidates []*loadbalance.Service) ([]*loadbalance.Service, *SelectionResult, error) {\n\tif len(candidates) == 0 {\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// If no health filter configured, pass through unchanged\n\tif s.filter == nil {\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\tbefore := len(candidates)\n\thealthy := s.filter.Filter(candidates)\n\n\t// Degrade, don't disappear: if every candidate is unhealthy, keep the full\n\t// set rather than emptying it — mirrors LoadBalancer.SelectService, so the\n\t// caller still gets a service (and the real upstream 429/auth) instead of a\n\t// \"no service available\" routing error.\n\tif before > 0 && len(healthy) == 0 {\n\t\tlogrus.WithContext(selectionLogContext(ctx)).WithFields(logrus.Fields{\n\t\t\t\"stage\":      \"routing_health_degrade\",\n\t\t\t\"rule_uuid\":  selectionRuleUUID(ctx),\n\t\t\t\"candidates\": before,\n\t\t}).Warnf(\"[health] all %d candidates unhealthy; keeping the full set (degrade)\", before)\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\tfilteredCount := before - len(healthy)\n\n\tif filteredCount > 0 {\n\t\tlogrus.WithContext(selectionLogContext(ctx)).WithFields(logrus.Fields{\n\t\t\t\"stage\":           \"routing_health_filtered\",\n\t\t\t\"rule_uuid\":       selectionRuleUUID(ctx),\n\t\t\t\"filtered_count\":  filteredCount,\n\t\t\t\"remaining_count\": len(healthy),\n\t\t\t\"candidate_count\": before,\n\t\t}).Warnf(\"[health] Filtered %d unhealthy services, %d remaining (of %d total)\",\n\t\t\tfilteredCount, len(healthy), before)\n\t\t// Log each filtered service for debugging\n\t\tfor _, svc := range candidates {\n\t\t\tif !s.filter.IsHealthy(svc.ServiceID()) {\n\t\t\t\tlogrus.WithContext(selectionLogContext(ctx)).WithFields(logrus.Fields{\n\t\t\t\t\t\"stage\":         \"routing_health_filtered_service\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"rule_uuid\":     selectionRuleUUID(ctx),\n\t\t\t\t\t\"service\":       svc.ServiceID(),\n\t\t\t\t\t\"provider_uuid\": svc.Provider,\n\t\t\t\t\t\"model\":         svc.Model,\n\t\t\t\t\t\"reason\":        \"rate_limited_or_auth_error\",\n\t\t\t\t}).Warnf(\"[health] Service %s:%s is unhealthy (rate limited/auth error)\",\n\t\t\t\t\tsvc.Provider, svc.Model)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Continue pipeline (don't select, just filter)\n\treturn healthy, nil, nil\n}\n\nfunc selectionLogContext(ctx *SelectionContext) context.Context {\n\tif ctx != nil && ctx.GinContext != nil && ctx.GinContext.Request != nil {\n\t\treturn ctx.GinContext.Request.Context()\n\t}\n\treturn context.Background()\n}\n\nfunc selectionRuleUUID(ctx *SelectionContext) string {\n\tif ctx != nil && ctx.Rule != nil {\n\t\treturn ctx.Rule.UUID\n\t}\n\treturn \"\"\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "internal/routing/stage_smart_routing.go",
      "content": "package routing\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\tpkgobs \"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/obs\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/ai/quota\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/constant\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/loadbalance\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/routing/smartrouting\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/typ\"\n)\n\n// QuotaProvider gives the smart-routing stage read access to quota usage\n// (ai/quota) so the service_quota position can compare against provider\n// usage. The stage only declares what it needs — usage for a provider —\n// and leaves freshness policy to the implementation (quota.Manager serves\n// stored data kept fresh by its background refresher). *quota.Manager\n// satisfies this.\ntype QuotaProvider interface {\n\tGetQuota(ctx context.Context, providerUUID string) (*quota.ProviderUsage, error)\n}\n\n// SmartRoutingStage evaluates smart routing rules and returns matched services.\n// If multiple services match, applies load balancing within the matched set.\ntype SmartRoutingStage struct {\n\taffinityStore AffinityStore\n\tquotaProvider QuotaProvider       // optional; wires service_quota ops to quota usage\n\tmultiLogger   *pkgobs.MultiLogger // optional; used to emit structured smart-routing logs\n}\n\n// NewSmartRoutingStage creates a new smart routing stage\nfunc NewSmartRoutingStage(affinity AffinityStore) *SmartRoutingStage {\n\treturn &SmartRoutingStage{affinityStore: affinity}\n}\n\n// SetMultiLogger attaches the multi-logger so the stage can emit structured\n// smart-routing evaluation logs viewable from the frontend system log page.\nfunc (s *SmartRoutingStage) SetMultiLogger(ml *pkgobs.MultiLogger) {\n\ts.multiLogger = ml\n}\n\n// SetQuotaProvider wires quota lookups into the stage. Optional —\n// when unset, service_quota ops see no data and pass through (see\n// evaluateServiceQuotaOp in internal/routing/smartrouting/routing.go).\nfunc (s *SmartRoutingStage) SetQuotaProvider(qp QuotaProvider) {\n\ts.quotaProvider = qp\n}\n\n// Name returns the stage identifier\nfunc (s *SmartRoutingStage) Name() string {\n\treturn SourceSmartRouting\n}\n\n// requestHeadLen is intentionally small — the per-op trace already records a\n// window around the matched substring (or a small head for non-text ops), so\n// the snapshot only needs to surface enough context to recognize *which*\n// request a row corresponds to. We avoid storing the full message bodies.\nconst requestHeadLen = 80\n\nfunc requestHead(s string) string {\n\tif len(s) <= requestHeadLen {\n\t\treturn s\n\t}\n\treturn s[:requestHeadLen] + \"…\"\n}\n\n// requestSnapshot captures key request fields used during smart routing\n// evaluation so operators can correlate decisions with what the request\n// actually looked like. Long message bodies are truncated to a short head;\n// the per-op trace owns the matched-substring windowing so we don't duplicate\n// large payloads in memory.\nfunc requestSnapshot(reqCtx *smartrouting.RequestContext) map[string]interface{} {\n\tif reqCtx == nil {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]interface{}{\n\t\t\"model\":            reqCtx.Model,\n\t\t\"thinking_enabled\": requestHead(reqCtx.GetLatestUserMessage()),\n\t\t\"system_msg_count\": len(reqCtx.SystemMessages),\n\t\t\"user_msg_count\":   len(reqCtx.UserMessages),\n\t}\n}\n\n// emitTrace writes a structured matchedServicesCount,\n\t\t\"final_active_count\": finalActiveCount,\n\t\t\"trace\":              trace,\n\t\t\"request\":            requestSnapshot(reqCtx),\n\t\t\"rules_total\":        len(ctx.Rule.SmartRouting),\n\t}\n\tif matched && matchedRuleIndex < len(trace) {\n\t\tfields[\"matched_rule_description\"] = trace[matchedRuleIndex].Description\n\t}\n\tif selectedService != nil {\n\t\tfields[\"selected_provider\"] = selectedService.Provider\n\t\tfields[\"selected_model\"] = selectedService.Model\n\t}\n\tif ctx.GinContext != nil {\n\t\tfields[\"client_ip\"] = outcome))\n\t}\n\tlogrus.WithFields(fields).Debugf(\"[smart_routing] %s\", outcome)\n}\n\nfunc formatTraceMessage(matched bool, idx int, model, outcome string) string {\n\tif matched {\n\t\treturn It\n// never terminates the pipeline (final is always nil) — it only decides\n// WHICH scope the next stages see. err != nil {\n\t\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[smart_routing] processor %s/%s error: %v\",\n\t\t\t\tcp.op.Position, cp.op.Operation, err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif ctx.BypassedSmartRules == nil {\n\t\tctx.BypassedSmartRules = make(map[int]struct{})\n\t}\n\tctx.BypassedSmartRules[matchedRuleIndex] = struct{}{}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// collectAllCapacityInfo collects seat-capacity info for all services across all smart routing rules.\n// Deduplicates by serviceID. evaluateRule will filter down to per-rule services.\nfunc (s *SmartRoutingStage) collectAllCapacityInfo(rules []smartrouting.SmartRouting) []smartrouting.ServiceCapacityInfo {\n\tseen := make(map[string]struct{})\n\tvar result []smartrouting.ServiceCapacityInfo\n\tfor _, r := range rules {\n\t\tfor _, svc := range r.Services {\n\t\t\tid := svc.ServiceID()\n\t\t\tif _, ok := seen[id]; ok {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tseen[id] = struct{}{}\n\n\t\t\tcap := 0\n\t\t\tif svc.ModelCapacity != nil {\n\t\t\t\tcap = *svc.ModelCapacity\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tactive := 0\n\t\t\tif s.affinityStore != nil {\n\t\t\t\tactive = s.affinityStore.CountByService(id)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tresult = append(result, smartrouting.ServiceCapacityInfo{\n\t\t\t\tServiceID:   id,\n\t\t\t\tCapacity:    cap,\n\t\t\t\tActiveCount: active,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn result\n}\n\n// collectAllQuotaInfo collects quota usage for all services across all\n// smart routing rules, keyed by each service's provider UUID (svc.Provider).\n// Deduplicates by serviceID and memoizes lookups per provider (services in\n// one pool usually share an account);       "content": "package routing\n\nimport (\n\t\"strconv\"\n\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/clock\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/loadbalance\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/typ\"\n)\n\n// AffinityStage checks if a session has a locked service from previous requests.\n// If found and valid, returns the locked service; otherwise passes to next stage.\n//\n// It runs AFTER SmartRoutingStage, so pins are scoped to the content partition\n// smart routing matched (see AffinitySessionKey): a session pinned inside one\n// smart subset cannot drag requests that match a different subset — content\n// routing decides the partition, affinity provides stickiness within it.\ntype AffinityStage struct {\n\tstore AffinityStore\n}\n\n// NewAffinityStage creates a new affinity stage backed by the given store\nfunc NewAffinityStage(store AffinityStore) *AffinityStage {\n\treturn &AffinityStage{store: store}\n}\n\n// AffinitySessionKey returns the affinity-store session key scoped to the\n// content partition smart routing matched: the bare session for the rule's\n// top-level pool (no match, index -1), or session + \"#sr<idx>\" inside a smart\n// subset. Partition-scoping is what lets one session hold independent pins\n// per request kind (e.g. a Claude Code main pin and a subagent pin), each\n// with its own prompt-cache continuity.\n//\n// The partition identity is the smart rule's index, the only stable handle\n// the config offers. Editing the rule list can renumber partitions and\n// mis-bucket existing pins; pins are in-memory with short TTLs, so this\n// self-heals within one TTL.\nfunc AffinitySessionKey(sessionID string, matchedSmartRuleIndex int) string {\n\tif matchedSmartRuleIndex < 0 {\n\t\treturn sessionID\n\t}\n\treturn sessionID + \"#sr\" + strconv.Itoa(matchedSmartRuleIndex)\n}\n\n// Name returns the stage identifier\nfunc (s *AffinityStage) Name() string {\n\treturn SourceAffinity\n}\n\n// Evaluate checks for locked service affinity\nfunc (s *AffinityStage) Evaluate(ctx *SelectionContext, candidates []*loadbalance.Service) ([]*loadbalance.Service, *SelectionResult, error) {\n\trule := ctx.Rule\n\n\t// Skip if affinity not enabled. Affinity is a load-balancing concern and\n\t// is independent of smart routing — it applies whenever a session can be\n\t// identified, regardless of rule.SmartEnabled.\n\tif !rule.AffinityEnabled() || ctx.SessionID.IsEmpty() {\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Look up the pin in the partition smart routing just matched (or the\n\t// top-level partition when nothing matched).\n\tentry, ok := s.store.Get(rule.UUID, AffinitySessionKey(ctx.SessionID.String(), ctx.MatchedSmartRuleIndex))\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Strict TTL: honor the pin only while the entry has not expired.\n\t// Once the lock expires, the session must re-enter the selection pipeline\n\t// and postProcess will create a new lock with a fresh TTL.\n\tif clock.Now().After(entry.ExpiresAt) {\n\t\tlogrus.Infof(\"[affinity] affinity entry for session %s expired at %s; dropping pin so strategy re-selects\",\n\t\t\tctx.SessionID.String(), entry.ExpiresAt)\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\tlogrus.Infof(\"[affinity] using locked service for session %s: %s\",\n\t\tctx.SessionID.String(), entry.Service.Model)\n\n\t// The candidate set is the scope this request may select from — the\n\t// pipeline driver keeps it non-empty whenever the rule has active\n\t// services, so an empty set means nothing is selectable here and the pin\n\t// must be declined (not trusted blindly), or a pin could leak an\n\t// out-of-scope service (e.g. a partition-only service into a\n\t// non-matching request whose base pool has no active services).\n\tif !ContainsService(candidates, entry.Service) {\n\t\tlogrus.Debugf(\"[affinity] locked service %s not in candidate set, skipping\",\n\t\t\tentry.Service.ServiceID())\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Health scoping (breaker-aware): only honor a pin while the locked service\n\t// is one the strategy would actually pick right now. This is driven by the\n\t// rule's config shape, not its tactic label — \"tier\" is just the emergent\n\t// shape of a multi-layer rule:\n\t//   - many layers: drop a pin to a fallback tier once the primary recovers.\n\t//   - one layer, many services: drop a pin to a dead peer when healthy\n\t//     peers exist.\n\t//   - one service: always honored (nothing else to pick).\n\t// On decline the pipeline falls through to the strategy, which re-selects a\n\t// currently-valid service, and postProcess re-pins the session there.\n\tif !typ.IsAffinityEligible(rule.UUID, candidates, entry.Service) {\n\t\tlogrus.Infof(\"[affinity] locked service %s is not currently selectable for session %s; dropping pin so strategy re-selects\",\n\t\t\tentry.Service.ServiceID(), ctx.SessionID.String())\n\t\treturn candidates, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\tresult := NewResult(entry.Service, SourceAffinity)\n\tresult.MatchedSmartRuleIndex = ctx.MatchedSmartRuleIndex\n\treturn candidates, result, nil\n}\n"
