      "content": "// Package aimodel — failover_dispatch.go\n//\n// Mid-request failover for the priority routing tactic, built as a\n// layered hand-off rather than a smart shim fused into the main path:\n//\n//   - Producer (the protocol handler) emits chunks normally, unaware of\n//     failover. On its first real stream chunk it raises one signal,\n//     CommitFirstChunk, and otherwise does nothing differently.\n//   - firstChunkGate is a passive, protocol-agnostic byte buffer. It\n//     makes no decisions: it records writes until CommitFirstChunk (or\n//     the orchestrator's terminal flush) lets them through.\n//   - Orchestrator (dispatchWithPriorityFailover) owns the retry\n//     decision. It reads the gate's committed/status state after each\n//     attempt and either commits, discards + retries the next tier, or\n//     flushes the buffered terminal error.\n//\n// Single-service requests skip the gate entirely, so the common case\n// never touches the buffer.\n\npackage protocolserver\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"maps\"\n\t\"net/http\"\n\n\t\"github.com/gin-gonic/gin\"\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/constant\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/recording\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/loadbalance\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/protocol\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/protocol/stream\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/typ\"\n)\n\n// preStreamErrorRecorder narrows the recorder contract to what\n// pre-stream failure sites need — both *ProtocolRecorder and\n// *streamRecorder fit.\ntype preStreamErrorRecorder interface {\n\tRecordError(error)\n}\n\n// handlePreStreamFailure emits the canonical \"upstream failed\n// pre-stream\" response: status 500 + JSON error, captured by the\n// buffered failover writer so the orchestrator can retry the next\n// priority tier.\nfunc (ph *ProtocolHandler) handlePreStreamFailure(c *gin.Context, err error, recorder preStreamErrorRecorder) {\n\tph.trackUsageFromContext(c, 0, 0, err)\n\tstream.SendStreamingError(c, err)\n\tif recorder != nil {\n\t\trecorder.RecordError(err)\n\t}\n}\n\n// failAttemptSetup reports an in-attempt setup failure — target/endpoint\n// resolution, the pre-transform chain, or the transform itself — that happens\n// before any upstream call. It always writes a 500-class status, which the\n// failover gate buffers and treats as retryable, so the orchestrator advances\n// to the next candidate (possibly a different API style) instead of terminating\n// the whole request on one misconfigured provider. Genuine client errors are\n// rejected in the prologue, before the gate is installed, so they remain\n// non-retryable and reach the client unchanged.\nfunc (ph *ProtocolHandler) FailAttemptSetup(c *gin.Context, err error) {\n\twriteErrorResponse(c, http.StatusInternalServerError, ErrorResponse{\n\t\tError: ErrorDetail{\n\t\t\tMessage: protocol.UpstreamMessage(err),\n\t\t\tType:    \"api_error\",\n\t\t},\n\t})\n}\n\n// retryableUpstreamStatuses are the HTTP status codes treated as\n// \"upstream transiently sick, try the next priority tier\".\n//\n// 500 is included because in-process error helpers (SendStreamingError,\n// SendErrorResponse on forwarding failure) wrap upstream pre-stream\n// errors as 500. 502 covers the explicit \"upstream stream failed\" path.\n// Keeping both means refactors that change one helper's status code\n// don't silently break failover.\n//\n// 401/403 are here because an upstream auth failure is a property of one\n// credential, not of the request: an OAuth token caught mid-refresh, a rotated\n// or revoked API key, a provider-side quota flag. The inbound caller's own\n// token is checked by middleware long before the gate is installed, so a 401\n// reaching this point always came from a provider — and answering it with a\n// sibling service is the whole reason a rule holds more than one. Without\n// this, a single stale credential turns into \"Please run /login\" on the\n// client while healthy services sit idle.\nvar retryableUpstreamStatuses = map[int]bool{\n\thttp.StatusUnauthorized:        true,\n\thttp.StatusForbidden:           true,\n\thttp.StatusTooManyRequests:     true,\n\thttp.StatusBadGateway:          true,\n\thttp.StatusServiceUnavailable:  true,\n\thttp.StatusGatewayTimeout:      true,\n\thttp.StatusInternalServerError: true,\n}\n\n// isRetryableStatus reports whether a buffered status code from a\n// dispatch attempt should trigger failover. Status 0 means the writer\n// was never touched — treat as terminal (the handler ran to completion\n// without writing, retrying would just repeat the no-op).\nfunc isRetryableStatus(status int) bool {\n\treturn status != 0 && retryableUpstreamStatuses[status]\n}\n\n// firstChunkGate is a passive, protocol-agnostic byte buffer placed\n// between a dispatch attempt and the real response writer. It makes no\n// decisions of its own: it records writes into a buffer until an\n// explicit signal commits them. The retry decision lives in the\n// orchestrator; the \"first real chunk arrived\" signal comes from the\n// streaming producer via CommitFirstChunk.\n//\n// Lifecycle:\n//   - buffered  — Write/WriteHeader capture into buf/hdr/status.\n//   - committed — after CommitFirstChunk or CommitIfBuffered, all I/O\n//     passes straight through to the real writer.\n//   - discarded — Discard resets the buffer for the next retry tier\n//     (valid only while uncommitted).\ntype firstChunkGate struct {\n\tgin.ResponseWriter\n\treal      gin.ResponseWriter\n\tbuf       bytes.Buffer\n\thdr       http.Header\n\tstatus    int\n\tcommitted bool\n}\n\nfunc newFirstChunkGate(w gin.ResponseWriter) *firstChunkGate {\n\treturn &firstChunkGate{\n\t\tResponseWriter: w,\n\t\treal:           w,\n\t\thdr:            http.Header{},\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Header() http.Header {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\treturn g.real.Header()\n\t}\n\treturn g.hdr\n}\n\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\treturn g.real.Write(p)\n\t}\n\tif g.status == 0 {\n\t\tg.status = http.StatusOK\n\t}\n\treturn g.buf.Write(p)\n}\n\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) WriteString(s string) (int, error) {\n\treturn g.Write([]byte(s))\n}\n\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) WriteHeader(code int) {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\tg.real.WriteHeader(code)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tg.status = code\n}\n\n// WriteHeaderNow is swallowed while buffered, delegated once committed.\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) WriteHeaderNow() {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\tg.real.WriteHeaderNow()\n\t}\n}\n\n// Flush is a no-op while buffered (so partial SSE can't leak past the\n// gate before commit) and delegates once committed (so streaming clients\n// keep getting incremental delivery). ProcessStream type-asserts the\n// writer for http.Flusher, so this method must exist concretely.\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Flush() {\n\tif !g.committed {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif f, ok := g.real.(http.Flusher); ok {\n\t\tf.Flush()\n\t}\n}\n\n// Status returns the captured status: 0 while untouched, the recorded\n// code otherwise (Write defaults it to 200). Once committed it reflects\n// the real writer. The orchestrator treats 0 as terminal (non-retryable).\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Status() int {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\treturn g.real.Status()\n\t}\n\treturn g.status\n}\n\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Size() int {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\treturn g.real.Size()\n\t}\n\treturn g.buf.Len()\n}\n\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Written() bool {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\treturn g.real.Written()\n\t}\n\treturn g.buf.Len() > 0 || g.status != 0\n}\n\n// Committed reports whether the gate has flushed to the wire. Once\n// committed, retry is impossible — bytes have left the process.\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Committed() bool {\n\treturn g.committed\n}\n\n// CommitFirstChunk is the producer's \"first real chunk arrived\" signal.\n// It flushes captured headers + status + buffered body to the real\n// writer and switches to pass-through. Idempotent.\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) CommitFirstChunk() {\n\tg.commit()\n}\n\n// CommitFirstChunkIfGate signals \"first real chunk arrived\" if w is\n// currently a *firstChunkGate (installed by DispatchWithPriorityFailover\n// when a rule has more than one active service), no-op otherwise. Exported\n// so callers outside this package that simulate a streaming success (e.g.\n// the load-balance dry-run simulator) can commit the gate without needing\n// firstChunkGate itself exported. Returns whether a gate was found and\n// committed.\nfunc CommitFirstChunkIfGate(w gin.ResponseWriter) bool {\n\tgate, ok := w.(*firstChunkGate)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tgate.CommitFirstChunk()\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// CommitIfBuffered is the orchestrator's deferred terminal flush of an\n// uncommitted buffered response (the last error after retries are\n// exhausted). No-op when already committed or never touched.\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) CommitIfBuffered() {\n\tif g.committed || (g.buf.Len() == 0 && g.status == 0) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tg.commit()\n}\n\n// commit copies captured headers, status, and body to the real writer\n// and enters pass-through mode. gin defers WriteHeader to the first\n// Write or WriteHeaderNow, so for body-less responses WriteHeaderNow is\n// forced explicitly.\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) commit() {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tg.committed = true\n\tdst := g.real.Header()\n\tmaps.Copy(dst, g.hdr)\n\tstatus := g.status\n\tif status == 0 {\n\t\tstatus = http.StatusOK\n\t}\n\tg.real.WriteHeader(status)\n\tif g.buf.Len() > 0 {\n\t\t_, _ = g.real.Write(g.buf.Bytes())\n\t\tg.buf.Reset()\n\t} else {\n\t\tg.real.WriteHeaderNow()\n\t}\n}\n\n// Discard resets captured state for the next retry tier. No-op once committed.\nfunc (g *firstChunkGate) Discard() {\n\tif g.committed {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tg.buf.Reset()\n\tg.status = 0\n\tfor k := range g.hdr {\n\t\tdelete(g.hdr, k)\n\t}\n}\n\n// selectFallbackService picks the next priority tier excluding services\n// already tried in this request. requireAPIStyle, when non-empty, restricts\n// candidates to one API style; callers that re-transform the request per\n// attempt pass \"\" so the pool can span heterogeneous styles\n// (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and failover can rotate freely across providers.\n//\n// Returns (nil, nil, nil) when no compatible candidate remains.\nfunc (ph *ProtocolHandler) selectFallbackService(\n\trule *typ.Rule,\n\texcluded map[string]bool,\n\trequireAPIStyle protocol.APIStyle,\n) (*typ.Provider, *loadbalance.Service, error) {\n\tavailable := make([]*loadbalance.Service, 0)\n\tcandidateProviders := make(map[string]*typ.Provider)\n\tfor _, svc := range rule.GetActiveServices() {\n\t\tif excluded[svc.ServiceID()] {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tp, err := ph.deps.Config.GetProviderByUUID(svc.Provider)\n\t\tif err != nil || p == nil {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif requireAPIStyle != \"\" && p.APIStyle != requireAPIStyle {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tavailable = append(available, svc)\n\t\tcandidateProviders[svc.ServiceID()] = p\n\t}\n\tif len(available) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\ttempRule := *rule\n\ttempRule.Services = available\n\n\t// Use tier-aware selection when the rule uses tier-based routing.\n\t// This ensures fallback respects tier ordering (T0 → T1 → T2...)\n\t// instead of using the generic load balancer which might select\n\t// any available service regardless of tier priority.\n\ttactic := rule.LBTactic.Instantiate()\n\tif tactic.GetType() == loadbalance.TacticTier {\n\t\t// TierTactic already handles tier-ordered selection with breaker awareness\n\t\tsvc := tactic.SelectService(&tempRule)\n\t\tif svc == nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, nil, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn candidateProviders[svc.ServiceID()], svc, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// For non-tier tactics, use the load balancer\n\tsvc, err := ph.deps.LoadBalancer.SelectService(&tempRule)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\tif svc == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, nil\n\t}\n\treturn candidateProviders[svc.ServiceID()], svc, nil\n}\n\n// dispatchAttempt is the per-attempt callback. It writes through\n// c.Writer, which is the gate during the failover loop.\ntype dispatchAttempt func(provider *typ.Provider, model string)\n\n// dispatchWithPriorityFailover runs `attempt` repeatedly, retrying on\n// retryable buffered failures until either the gate commits (the\n// stream's first real chunk reached the wire, retry impossible) or the\n// candidate pool is exhausted (the last buffered error flushes on the\n// deferred return).\n//\n// Single-service requests bypass the gate entirely: with no fallback\n// tier, failover is impossible and there is no reason to buffer.\nfunc (ph *ProtocolHandler) DispatchWithPriorityFailover(\n\tc *gin.Context,\n\trule *typ.Rule,\n\tinitialProvider *typ.Provider,\n\tinitialModel string,\n\tattempt dispatchAttempt,\n) {\n\tactiveServices := rule.GetActiveServices()\n\tif len(activeServices) <= 1 {\n\t\tattempt(initialProvider, initialModel)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\trealWriter := c.Writer\n\tgate := newFirstChunkGate(realWriter)\n\tc.Writer = gate\n\tdefer func() {\n\t\tc.Writer = realWriter\n\t\tgate.CommitIfBuffered()\n\t}()\n\n\ttried := map[string]bool{}\n\tprovider := initialProvider\n\tmodel := initialModel\n\n\t// Keep the recorder's bound service in sync per attempt so the\n\t// breaker store gets fed the right serviceID on failure.\n\trec, _ := recording.GetRecorderFromContext(c)\n\n\tfor i := 0; i < len(activeServices); i++ {\n\t\tserviceID := loadbalance.FormatServiceID(provider.UUID, model)\n\t\ttried[serviceID] = true\n\n\t\t// Update \"breaker_failure_recorded\"\n\t\tfields[\"rule_uuid\"] = rule.UUID\n\t\tfields[\"status\"] = status\n\t\tfields[\"breaker_state\"] =       "content": "package protocolserver\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"net/http\"\n\n\t\"github.com/gin-gonic/gin\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/ai/quota\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/constant\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/typ\"\n)\n\n// QuotaReader reads stored provider quota; it never fetches upstream, so the\n// quota endpoint cannot drive requests to the vendors behind this box.\ntype QuotaReader interface {\n\tGetQuota(ctx context.Context, providerUUID string) (*quota.ProviderUsage, error)\n}\n\n// HandleScenarioQuota serves GET /tingly/:scenario[/v1]/quota: the quota of\n// the providers behind the scenario's rules, relayed as one\n// ProviderUsage for a downstream tingly-box to display\n// (.design/quota-relay.md). Only the owner's model token reads it; sharing\n// keys are refused until a team can opt in.\nfunc (ph *ProtocolHandler) HandleScenarioQuota(c *gin.Context) {\n\tif c.GetString(constant.CtxKeyAuthKind) == constant.AuthKindSharingKey {\n\t\twriteErrorResponse(c, http.StatusForbidden, ErrorResponse{Error: ErrorDetail{Message: \"Quota is not shared with sharing keys\", Type: \"forbidden_error\"}})\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif ph.deps.QuotaReader == nil {\n\t\twriteErrorResponse(c, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, ErrorResponse{Error: ErrorDetail{Message: \"Quota is not available on this server\", Type: \"service_unavailable\"}})\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tscenario := typ.RuleScenario(c.Param(\"scenario\"))\n\tseen := make(map[string]bool)\n\tvar upstreams []*quota.ProviderUsage\n\tfor _, rule := range ph.deps.Config.GetRequestConfigs() {\n\t\tif !rule.Active || rule.GetScenario() != scenario {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, svc := range rule.GetServices() {\n\t\t\tif svc == nil || !svc.Active || seen[svc.Provider] {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tseen[svc.Provider] = true\n\t\t\tif usage, err := ph.deps.QuotaReader.GetQuota(c.Request.Context(), svc.Provider); err == nil {\n\t\t\t\tupstreams = append(upstreams, usage)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tc.JSON(http.StatusOK, quota.RelayUsage(upstreams))\n}\n"

      "path": "internal/config/config.go",
      "content": "package config\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/hex\"\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io/ioutil\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"slices\"\n\t\"sync\"\n\n\t\"github.com/google/uuid\"\n\t\"github.com/sirupsen/logrus\"\n\t\"golang.org/x/crypto/sha3\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/catalog\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/constant\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/db\"\n\tguardrailsutils \"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/guardrails/utils\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/loadbalance\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/internal/typ\"\n\t\"github.com/tingly-dev/tingly-box/pkg/auth\"\n)\n\n// Config represents the global configuration\ntype Config struct {\n\t// Rules is the in-memory working set of routing rules. It is hydrated from\n\t// SQLite (db.RuleStore) at startup and written back through Save(); it is\n\t// deliberately NOT serialized to config.json anymore — the database is the\n\t// authority. The in-memory copy stays because the hot request path matches\n\t// rules under RLock and services carry hydrated runtime stats.\n\tRules []typ.Rule `yaml:\"rules\" json:\"-\"`\n\t// LegacyRules receives the file's \"rules\" array on load. It is consumed\n\t// exactly once, by hydrateRulesFromStore (one-time import into the\n\t// database on upgraded installs); after hydration the field stays nil and\n\t// file rules are ignored on reload. The \"rules\" key is no longer mirrored\n\t// by Save() (dual-write removed): it is read only for the legacy import and\n\t// written back as null.\n\tLegacyRules        []typ.Rule           `yaml:\"-\" json:\"rules\"`\n\tUserToken          string               `yaml:\"user_token\" json:\"user_token\"`               // User token for UI and control API authentication\n\tModelToken         string               `yaml:\"model_token\" json:\"model_token\"`             // Model token for OpenAI and Anthropic API authentication\n\tInternalAPIToken   string               `json:\"-\"`                                          // Internal API token for probe testing (generated at startup, not persisted)\n\tEncryptProviders   bool                 `yaml:\"encrypt_providers\" json:\"encrypt_providers\"` // Whether to encrypt provider info (default false)\n\tScenarios          []typ.ScenarioConfig `yaml:\"scenarios\" json:\"scenarios\"`                 // Scenario-specific configurations\n\tGUI                GUIConfig            `json:\"gui\"`                                        // GUI-specific settings\n\tRandomUUID         string               `json:\"random_uuid\"`                                // A random uuid to help protocol transform for some special provider\n\tClaudeCodeDeviceID string               `json:\"claude_code_device_id\"`                      // Calc from random claude code device id with sha256\n\n\t// Merged fields from Config struct\n\t// ProvidersV1 and Providers are legacy JSON-config storage for providers.\n\t// Providers now live in SQLite (db.ProviderStore); these fields are only\n\t// populated on load for one-time migration to the database and are cleared\n\t// by migrateProvidersToDB. The non-omitempty tags ensure that clearing them\n\t// results in a JSON null that overrides any stale value in the existing file.\n\tProvidersV1 map[string]*typ.Provider `json:\"providers\"`\n\tProviders   []*typ.Provider          `json:\"providers_v2\"`\n\tServerPort  int                      `json:\"-\"`\n\tServerHost  string                   `json:\"-\"` // Server host address (e.g., \"localhost\", \"0.0.0.0\", \"192.168.1.100\")\n\tJWTSecret   string                   `json:\"jwt_secret\"`\n\n\t// ProjectsDir is the Projects data directory chosen with --projects-dir,\n\t// remembered so a later start or restart without the flag keeps using it.\n\t// Empty means \"<config dir>-project\".\n\tProjectsDir string `json:\"projects_dir,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// Server settings\n\tDefaultMaxTokens int  `json:\"default_max_tokens\"` // Default max_tokens for anthropic API requests\n\tVerbose          bool `json:\"verbose\"`            // Verbose mode for detailed logging\n\tDebug            bool `json:\"-\"`                  // Debug mode for Gin debug level logging\n\tOpenBrowser      bool `yaml:\"-\" json:\"-\"`         // Auto-open browser in web UI mode (default: true)\n\n\t// UIPrefs holds small, UI-only preferences (which agents are hidden,\n\t// Quick Start progress, ...) so the browser tab and the desktop window —\n\t// two different origins with separate localStorage — see the same state.\n\t// Values are opaque JSON owned by the frontend; see ui_prefs.go.\n\t// Not omitempty: Save() keeps file keys missing from the marshalled\n\t// config, so clearing the map must serialize as null to stick.\n\tUIPrefs map[string]json.RawMessage `json:\"ui_prefs\"`\n\n\t// Generic tool configs map for all tool types\n\t// Key is tool_type (e.g., \"tool_interceptor\", \"code_execution\")\n\t// Value is the JSON-encoded config for that tool type\n\tToolConfigs map[string]json.RawMessage `json:\"tool_configs,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// Health monitor settings\n\tHealthMonitor loadbalance.HealthMonitorConfig `json:\"health_monitor,omitempty\" yaml:\"health_monitor,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// Profiles stores scenario profile metadata, keyed by base scenario name.\n\t// Each entry is a list of profiles for that scenario.\n\tProfiles map[string][]typ.ProfileMeta `json:\"profiles\" yaml:\"profiles\"`\n\n\t// Enterprise context JWT validation settings for TBE->TB proxy calls.\n\tEnterpriseContextJWT EnterpriseContextJWTConfig `json:\"enterprise_context_jwt,omitempty\" yaml:\"enterprise_context_jwt,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// HTTP Transport settings for upstream API connections\n\tHTTPTransport HTTPTransportConfig `json:\"http_transport,omitempty\" yaml:\"http_transport,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// Generic MCP path feature flags\n\t// When enabled, routes traffic through the new generic MCP architecture\n\tGenericMCP GenericMCPConfig `json:\"generic_mcp,omitempty\" yaml:\"generic_mcp,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// ProviderTemplateSource supports three modes:\n\t// 1. Empty/default -> use embedded templates (default GitHub sync behavior)\n\t// 2. file:///path/to/template.json -> load from local file\n\t// 3. https://example.com/template.json -> load from HTTP URL\n\tProviderTemplateSource string `yaml:\"provider_template_source,omitempty\" json:\"provider_template_source,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// MultiTenantConfig holds settings for multi-tenant API token authentication\n\tMultiTenantConfig MultiTenantConfig `yaml:\"multi_tenant,omitempty\" json:\"multi_tenant,omitempty\"`\n\n\t// MigrationsCompleted tracks which one-time migrations have already been applied.\n\t// This prevents idempotency-breaking migrations (e.g. service auto-fill) from\n\t// re-running on every restart and overwriting intentional user changes.\n\tMigrationsCompleted []string `json:\"migrations_completed,omitempty\" yaml:\"migrations_completed,omitempty\"`\n\n\tConfigFile string `yaml:\"-\" json:\"-\"` // Not serialized to YAML (exported to preserve field)\n\tConfigDir  string `yaml:\"-\" json:\"-\"`\n\n\tmodelManager *catalog.ModelListManager\n\tstoreManager *db.StoreManager // Unified store manager for all database stores\n\n\t// Store references for internal Config methods (RefreshStatsFromStore, etc.)\n\t// External consumers should use StoreManager() instead\n\tstatsStore         *db.StatsStore\n\tusageStore         *db.UsageStore\n\tproviderStore      *db.ProviderStore\n\timbotSettingsStore *db.ImBotSettingsStore\n\ttemplateManager    *catalog.ProviderCatalogManager\n\n\t// credentialStore backs the guardrails protected-credential database,\n\t// which is a separate file from tingly.db. Built lazily by\n\t// CredentialStore.\n\tcredentialStore *guardrailsutils.ProtectedCredentialStore\n\n\t// Provider lifecycle hooks\n\tproviderUpdateHooks []ProviderUpdateHook\n\tproviderDeleteHooks []ProviderDeleteHook\n\thookMu              sync.RWMutex\n\n\t// rulesHydrated flips once hydrateRulesFromStore has run; after that,\n\t// rules appearing in config.json (e.g. hand edits picked up by the\n\t// watcher's hot reload) are ignored — the database is authoritative.\n\trulesHydrated bool\n\t// lastSyncedRules caches the JSON snapshot of Rules from the last\n\t// successful store sync so Save() calls that didn't touch rules skip the\n\t// database write entirely. Guarded by ruleSyncMu, not mu: several Save()\n\t// call sites run without holding mu, so the sync bookkeeping needs its\n\t// own lock to serialize concurrent Save() calls.\n\tlastSyncedRules []byte\n\truleSyncMu      sync.Mutex\n\n\tmu sync.RWMutex\n}\n\n// ConfigOption is a function that modifies a Config during initialization\ntype ConfigOption func(*configOptions)\n\n// configOptions holds the options for creating a new Config\ntype configOptions struct {\n\tconfigDir       string\n\tenableMigration bool\n\tenableBuiltIn   bool\n}\n\n// WithConfigDir returns a ConfigOption that sets a custom config directory\nfunc WithConfigDir(dir string) ConfigOption {\n\treturn func(opts *configOptions) {\n\t\topts.configDir = dir\n\t}\n}\n\n// WithDisableMigration returns a ConfigOption that disables the migration step\n// Useful when using tingly-box as a library in external projects\nfunc WithDisableMigration() ConfigOption {\n\treturn func(opts *configOptions) {\n\t\topts.enableMigration = false\n\t}\n}\n\n// WithDisableBuiltIn returns a ConfigOption that disables the built-in rules creation\nfunc WithDisableBuiltIn() ConfigOption {\n\treturn func(opts *configOptions) {\n\t\topts.enableBuiltIn = false\n\t}\n}\n\n// NewDefaultConfig creates a new global configuration manager with default settings\n// Uses the default tingly config directory and runs migrations\nfunc NewDefaultConfig() (*Config, error) {\n\tconfigDir := constant.GetTinglyConfDir()\n\tif configDir == \"\" {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"config directory is empty\")\n\t}\n\n\tallOpts := []ConfigOption{}\n\tallOpts = append(allOpts, WithConfigDir(configDir))\n\treturn NewConfig(allOpts...)\n}\n\n// NewConfig creates a new global configuration manager with the given options\n// If no config directory is specified, uses the default tingly config directory\nfunc NewConfig(opts ...ConfigOption) (*Config, error) {\n\t// Apply options\n\toptions := &configOptions{\n\t\tconfigDir:       \"\", // Will be set to default if empty\n\t\tenableMigration: true,\n\t\tenableBuiltIn:   true,\n\t}\n\tfor _, opt := range opts {\n\t\topt(options)\n\t}\n\n\t// Use default config directory if not specified\n\tconfigDir := options.configDir\n\tif configDir == \"\" {\n\t\tconfigDir = constant.GetTinglyConfDir()\n\t\tif configDir == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"config directory is empty\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tif err := os.MkdirAll(configDir, 0700); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create cfg directory: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\tconfigFile := filepath.Join(configDir, \"config.json\")\n\tif configFile == \"\" {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"cfg file path is empty\")\n\t}\n\n\tcfg := &Config{\n\t\tConfigFile: configFile,\n\t\tConfigDir:  configDir,\n\t}\n\n\t// Initialize unified store manager (initializes all stores in one call)\n\tstoreManager, err := db.NewStoreManager(configDir)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to initialize store manager: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tcfg.storeManager = storeManager\n\n\t// Cache store references for internal Config methods\n\tcfg.statsStore = storeManager.Stats()\n\tcfg.usageStore = storeManager.Usage()\n\tcfg.providerStore = storeManager.Provider()\n\tcfg.imbotSettingsStore = storeManager.ImBotSettings()\n\n\t// Load existing cfg if exists\n\tif err := cfg.load(); err != nil {\n\t\t// If file doesn't exist, create default cfg\n\t\tif os.IsNotExist(err) {\n\t\t\terr = cfg.CreateDefaultConfig()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to load global cfg: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Hydrate rules from the database (or migrate legacy JSON rules into it).\n\t// Must run before Migrate so migration steps operate on the real rule set.\n\t// Like migrateProvidersToDB, this is storage plumbing rather than a config\n\t// migration, so it is not gated by enableMigration.\n\tif err := cfg.hydrateRulesFromStore(); err != nil {\n\t\t// Don't leak the SQLite handles of a Config the caller never receives.\n\t\t_ = cfg.CloseStores()\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to hydrate rules from store: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\t// Run migration only once at startup (not on every load/reload)\n\t// Skip migration if disabled (useful when using as a library)\n\tif !options.enableMigration {\n\t\tlogrus.Warnf(\"migration disabled\")\n\t} else {\n\t\tMigrate(cfg)\n\t\tif err := cfg.Save(); err != nil {\n\t\t\tlogrus.WithError(err).Warn(\"Failed to persist config after migration; in-memory state may diverge until the next successful save\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Built-in rules setup\n\tif !options.enableBuiltIn {\n\t\tlogrus.Warnf(\"built-in rules disabled\")\n\t} else {\n\t\tcfg.InsertDefaultRule()\n\t}\n\n\t// Ensure tokens exist even for existing configs\n\tupdated := false\n\tif cfg.JWTSecret == \"\" {\n\t\tcfg.JWTSecret = generateSecret()\n\t\tupdated = true\n\t}\n\tif cfg.UserToken == \"\" {\n\t\t// Always generate a cryptographically secure random token for new installs.\n\t\t// Falling back to a well-known default would defeat the purpose, so fail loudly instead.\n\t\tuserToken, err := GenerateUserToken()\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to generate secure user token: %w\", Reads the field directly (not via c.StoreManager()) —\n// callers may already hold c.mu, and the field is only ever set during\n// construction.\nfunc (c *Config) rulesStore() *db.RuleStore {\n\tif c.storeManager == nil {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn c.storeManager.Rules()\n}\n\n// hydrateRulesFromStore populates Config.Rules at startup, migrating legacy\n// config.json rules into the database the first time it runs on an upgraded\n// install. A non-empty rules array in the file\n\t\t// (a hand edit, or a leftover mirror from a pre-removal version) is\n\t\t// not an input anymore; the next Save() nulls it. Divergent content\n\t\t// means rule changes were made outside this version's control —\n\t\t// those changes are NOT merged back; say so loudly instead of\n\t\t// discarding them in silence.\n\t\tif len(legacy) > 0 && !rulesEquivalent(legacy, stored) {\n\t\t\tlogrus.Warnf(\"config.json rules differ from the database (%d in file, %d in database); See\n// https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/providers.\n\n// dshGatewayProviderName is the tingly-box provider key written into\n// settings.yaml's `llm-pi-ai.providers` map by mergeDshSettings.\nconst dshGatewayProviderName = \"tingly-box\"\n\n// dshAPIKeyEnvName is the env var name settings.yaml's apiKeyEnv points at,\n// and the key written into .credentials.yaml. Fixed rather than\n// user-configurable: it's an implementation detail of dsh's credential\n// indirection, not a user-tunable knob.\nconst dshAPIKeyEnvName = \"TINGLY_BOX_API_KEY\"\n\n// dshHomeDir resolves $DSH_HOME, falling back to ~/.dsh when unset (dsh's\n// docs do not state a default; ~/.dsh follows the common single-dotdir\n// convention used by similar CLIs).\nfunc dshHomeDir() (string, error) {\n\tif v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(\"DSH_HOME\")); v != \"\" {\n\t\treturn v, nil\n\t}\n\thome, err := os.UserHomeDir()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"failed to get home directory: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif home == \"\" {\n\t\treturn \"\", fmt.Errorf(\"home directory resolved to empty path\")\n\t}\n\treturn filepath.Join(home, \".dsh\"), nil\n}\n\n// DshPrefs is the typed, user-tunable surface of settings.yaml's tingly-box\n// provider entry. DefaultInput mirrors the provider-level `defaultInput` key\n// (\"text\" or \"text_image\" -> [text] / [text, image]); empty omits the key so\n// dsh treats the provider as text-only — the conservative default for models\n// tingly-box cannot verify support vision (same stance as Codex's third-party\n// defaults, see .design/codex-config.md). Chosen for backward\n// compatibility: it's the value this stanza always wrote before Protocol\n// became user-tunable.\nconst dshDefaultProtocol = \"openai-completions\"\n\n// dshProtocolValues lists the wire protocols dsh's llm-pi-ai adapter can\n// describe with just a key, an endpoint, and headers (its `supportedProtocols()`\n// — see packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/provider.ts in deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).\nvar dshProtocolValues = []string{\"openai-completions\", \"openai-responses\", \"anthropic-messages\"}\n\n// dshProtocolValue validates val against dshProtocolValues, returning the\n// trimmed value and true when it is a member, or \"\"/false otherwise (empty\n// input also yields false).
